test_issue: An appeal should not be treated as abated where the opposing party was not duly notified of the respondent’s death and the delay in seeking substitution therefore cannot fairly be attributed to the appellant.
rule_question: When a party to a pending appeal dies and the legal representatives are not substituted within the prescribed time, does the appeal abate, and if so, does the abatement extend only to the deceased party's interest or to the whole appeal?
rule_statement: Where a party to a pending appeal dies and no timely substitution is made, the appeal abates automatically as to that party and the decree becomes final against that party's side. Abatement extends to the whole appeal only where the decree or interest is joint and indivisible, or success for the survivors would produce contradictory decrees, or effective relief cannot be granted without the deceased party. Where interests are separate and severable, the appeal continues as to the others.
rule_if: appeal_pending and party_to_appeal_dies and legal_representatives_not_substituted_in_time and abatement_not_set_aside

test_issue: Possession cannot be transferred to the acquiring trust before it deposits the compensation determined under the governing statute.
rule_question: Once land or a proprietary or intermediary interest in it has vested in the State (by completed acquisition or by land-reform, ceiling or surplus legislation), can the former owner or proprietor recover possession, restitution, reconveyance or related relief, or does the vesting bar the claim?
rule_statement: Once land or a proprietary interest has validly vested in the State, whether through completed acquisition or through land-reform, ceiling or surplus legislation, the former owner cannot recover possession, restitution, reconveyance or related relief. This holds even if the land is unused, put to another public purpose, or not yet used, unless a statutory saving or a statutory reconveyance condition is satisfied.

test_issue: Criminal proceedings may be quashed under the court’s inherent powers when the allegations, even taken at face value, do not prima facie disclose an offence.
rule_question: Can a High Court, in exercise of its inherent or writ jurisdiction, quash an FIR, investigation, charge-sheet or criminal proceeding at the threshold where the allegations, taken at face value, disclose an offence and the accused's defence, the reliability of the allegations or the accused's involvement depends on disputed facts or evidence that has yet to be collected or tested?
rule_statement: A court exercising inherent or writ jurisdiction to quash criminal proceedings must examine the allegations and material at face value and must not weigh evidence, test reliability, or decide disputed defences. Where the allegations disclose an offence and the outcome depends on disputed facts or incomplete investigation, and no exceptional ground is made out, the proceeding must continue.
rule_if: criminal_proceeding_quashing_challenge and allegations_taken_at_face_value_disclose_offence and (truth_reliability_or_defence_depends_on_disputed_facts_or_evidence or investigation_incomplete) and not exceptional_ground_for_quashing_made_out

test_issue: In proceedings under Order XXI Rules 97–101 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an executing court cannot determine title claims by third parties asserting independent title; it may assess whether their claim is bona fide and independent.
rule_question: Where a person who is not bound by a possession decree resists delivery of possession in execution by asserting an independent right or interest in the property, must the executing court adjudicate that claim under Order XXI Rules 97-103 CPC before dispossession, instead of rejecting it as non-maintainable or relegating the person to a post-dispossession remedy?
rule_statement: A person who is not bound by a possession decree and who resists delivery by asserting an independent right in the property is entitled to have the claim heard and decided by the executing court in the execution proceedings under Order XXI Rules 97-103 CPC. The objector need not first be dispossessed, and the court cannot reject the objection summarily or on non-maintainability grounds without adjudicating it.
rule_if: execution_of_decree_for_possession and objector_not_bound_by_decree and objector_claims_independent_right_in_property and objector_resists_or_obstructs_delivery

test_issue: Mutation entries in revenue records do not create or confer title to property.
rule_question: Where a transfer of immovable property must be made by a registered instrument, can an oral sale, an agreement or contract to sell, an unregistered document, or delivery of possession alone transfer title or create an interest in the property before a registered conveyance is completed?
rule_statement: A sale of immovable property that the law requires to be made by registered instrument transfers title only when the registered conveyance is complete. An oral sale, an agreement to sell, an unregistered document, or possession or part-payment alone does not transfer title or create an interest in the property. A contract to sell gives at most a personal right, for example to seek specific performance.
rule_if: immovable_property_transfer_claimed and transfer_requires_registered_instrument and claim_rests_on_non_conveyance_basis and not registered_conveyance_completed

test_issue: A conviction under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code cannot stand when fewer than five persons are found to have formed an unlawful assembly.
rule_question: Must a conviction for an offence founded on group or constructive liability (common intention or unlawful assembly), or on an individual attributed act, be set aside where the evidence does not reliably prove the accused's own participation, shared intention or common object, or where the facts negate the offence, for instance private defence or no death caused?
rule_statement: A conviction resting on common intention, unlawful assembly or an attributed individual act cannot be sustained unless reliable evidence proves the accused's own participation and, for constructive liability, the shared intention or common object. It also fails where the conduct was private defence or an essential element of the offence is missing. The prosecution must prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt, and doubt goes to the accused.
rule_if: appeal_from_conviction and (prosecution_evidence_does_not_reliably_establish_accused_participation_or_role or shared_intention_or_common_object_not_proved or (acts_done_in_private_defence and not private_defence_exceeded_for_injury_offences) or essential_ingredient_of_offence_absent) and not other_reliable_evidence_independently_establishes_guilt

test_issue: Whether the failure of a principal heir to testify affected the defendants’ case.
rule_question: What is the effect of the prosecution's failure to explain injuries sustained by an accused in the same occurrence: does it require rejection of, or reasonable doubt about, the prosecution case, or can the case stand where the injuries are minor or the prosecution evidence is clear, cogent and credible?
rule_statement: Non-explanation of an accused's injuries is a relevant circumstance but not by itself fatal to the prosecution. The prosecution case stands where the injuries are minor, or the injuries are shown to be unconnected or self-inflicted, or the prosecution evidence is clear, cogent and credible. It is materially undermined, with benefit of doubt or acquittal, where serious injuries in the same occurrence are unexplained and the prosecution evidence is unreliable or interested, the defence account is plausible, or the origin of the occurrence is suppressed.
rule_if: criminal_case and accused_sustained_injuries_in_occurrence and prosecution_did_not_explain_injuries and (injuries_minor_or_superficial or prosecution_evidence_clear_cogent_and_credible or injuries_shown_self_inflicted_or_unconnected_to_occurrence) and not (injuries_serious_and_prosecution_evidence_unreliable_or_defence_account_plausible_or_origin_of_occurrence_suppressed)

test_issue: A valid gift requires acceptance by or on behalf of the donee, and a registered gift deed without evidence of acceptance is null and void.
rule_question: Is a gift of agricultural land, made without valuable consideration (only love and affection), a transfer for consideration within the statutory exception that protects transfers from land-ceiling and surplus-land provisions?
rule_statement: A gift is by definition a voluntary transfer without consideration, and natural love and affection is not legal consideration. A gift therefore cannot come within a land-ceiling exception that protects only transfers for (adequate) consideration, and the land is counted in determining surplus area.
rule_if: land_ceiling_proceeding and land_transferred_by_gift and not valuable_consideration_given and statute_exception_requires_consideration

test_issue: Whether the consolidation authorities could treat the leased land as joint-family property and apply Hindu-law principles to determine the shares of Muslim parties.
rule_question: When property is held in the name of a member of a joint Hindu family, who bears the burden of proving whether it is joint family property or self-acquired, and when does proof of an adequate joint family nucleus shift that burden?
rule_statement: Proof that a Hindu family is joint does not by itself make a member's acquisitions joint, and the party asserting joint ownership must first prove an adequate family nucleus. Once that nucleus is shown, the burden shifts to the member claiming self-acquisition to prove acquisition without family aid, and if he fails the property is joint family property. If no adequate nucleus is shown, the claim fails.
rule_if: joint_family_exists and property_held_in_family_member_name and property_claimed_as_joint_family_property and claimant_proved_adequate_nucleus_capable_of_funding_acquisition and not holder_proved_acquisition_without_family_aid

test_issue: An authorized officer may extend the time for an auction purchaser to pay the balance sale price within the statutory maximum period, but the purchaser has no right to an extension, and refusal is reviewable where exceptional circumstances show the decision-making process was arbitrary or unreasonable.
rule_question: Does a court retain power to extend a time it has fixed for a procedural or decretal step, such as payment, deposit or fee, even after the time has expired, and on what considerations is that discretion exercised?
rule_statement: A court that has fixed a time for a step in a proceeding or decree, particularly a specific performance decree, which is treated as preliminary until the sale deed is executed, keeps the power to extend that time even after it expires. The power is discretionary and turns on the applicant's conduct, bona fides, and the circumstances, so an extension can be refused where the applicant was dilatory.
rule_if: court_fixed_time_for_compliance_step and time_limit_fixed_by_court_or_decree and (compliance_proceeding_still_pending_or_decree_not_fully_executed) and request_or_occasion_for_extension

test_issue: An appellate court cannot remand a case merely because it considers the evidence on record insufficient or because a party failed to produce evidence.
rule_question: Can a party obtain, at the appellate or later stage, relief, a finding or a remand that depends on a claim that was never pleaded or relief that was never sought, or on evidence that was available but not adduced below, when no recognised ground (amendment, prevention despite due diligence, or need for the court to pronounce judgment) is shown?
rule_statement: A court decides a dispute on the case pleaded and the evidence led in the proceedings below. On appeal it will not grant unpleaded or unrequested relief, and it will not admit or remand for evidence that was available but not produced, unless a recognised ground such as prevention despite due diligence, need for the evidence to pronounce judgment, or a proper amendment is shown.

test_issue: Whether a court exercising jurisdiction under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act may set aside an arbitral award after it has been upheld under Section 34 when the tribunal’s contractual interpretation is a plausible view.
rule_question: Within the limited grounds on which an arbitral award may be challenged, can a court set aside or disturb an award by reappraising evidence, re-examining the merits, or correcting alleged errors of fact or application of law that disclose no statutory ground or error on the face of the award?
rule_statement: A court reviewing an arbitral award does not sit in appeal. It cannot set the award aside by reappraising evidence, re-examining the merits, inferring reasons from a non-speaking award, or accepting objections outside the statutory grounds, unless a recognised ground or an error on the face of the award is established.

test_issue: Misuse of official authority or deviation from government policy, without material alleging demand and acceptance or obtainment of illegal gratification, does not by itself establish an offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
rule_question: Can a court direct or refer a matter for investigation against a public official where the legal preconditions for that step, namely a prima facie finding of an offence or the prior sanction required by statute, have not been met?
rule_statement: A court may not order or refer an investigation against a public official as a fishing inquiry to see whether an offence exists, without a prima facie finding of an offence. Where the alleged offence is a protected corruption offence against a public servant, a referral for investigation, including under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., also requires valid prior sanction under Section 19(1) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

test_issue: A writ petition seeking the same relief as a civil suit withdrawn without liberty to file afresh is barred by constructive res judicata.
rule_question: Does a final decision on the merits by a competent court or tribunal, including in a constitutional writ proceeding or quasi-judicial proceeding that is not itself a suit, bar the same parties or their privies from relitigating the same issue or matter in a later proceeding?
rule_statement: Res judicata rests on public policy and finality and is not confined to the technical terms of Section 11 CPC. A final merits decision of a competent court, writ court or quasi-judicial tribunal binds the same parties or their privies on the same issue in later proceedings, unless it has been reversed or modified through an appropriate remedy.
rule_if: prior_competent_forum_decision_on_merits and prior_decision_final_not_reversed_or_modified and same_parties_or_privies and same_issue_or_matter_directly_decided and later_proceeding_seeks_to_relitigate

test_issue: Whether the suit property remained coparcenary property and was available for partition when the state amendment granting unmarried daughters coparcenary status came into force.
rule_question: When a male Hindu coparcener dies after the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 commenced, leaving a Class I female heir, does his interest in Mitakshara coparcenary property devolve by succession rather than survivorship, how is it quantified, and what do the heirs take?
rule_statement: Under the proviso and Explanation 1 to Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, a deceased coparcener's interest passes by succession, not survivorship, when a Class I female heir survives him. The interest is fixed by a notional partition immediately before death, and the fiction is carried through fully. A female entitled to a share on that partition therefore receives it in addition to her share as an heir. The heirs hold their inherited shares individually, not as joint family property.

test_issue: Whether the balance consideration payable for specific performance should be increased in view of the circumstances of the defendants.
rule_question: In a suit for discretionary specific performance of an agreement to sell immovable property, does delay by the claimant (including delay within the limitation period and a rise in property value) justify refusing relief, or does refusal require something more, such as claimant conduct or neglect, prejudice to the other side or third parties, waiver, or other inequity?
rule_statement: Where a specific performance suit is filed within limitation, delay alone, including delay caused by court proceedings or a mere rise in property value, is not a ground to refuse the remedy. Relief may be refused, or made conditional on a higher price, only where the delay is coupled with claimant conduct or neglect, prejudice, waiver, or other circumstances that make enforcement inequitable, and this is assessed on the totality of the facts.
rule_if: specific_performance_suit and suit_within_limitation and delay_relied_on_to_refuse_relief and not claimant_conduct_or_neglect_made_relief_inequitable and not delay_caused_prejudice_waiver_or_third_party_rights

test_issue: A valid compulsory acquisition under Article 300A requires more than acquisition authority and fair compensation; it must include procedures protecting the rights to notice, hearing, a reasoned decision, public purpose, restitution or fair compensation, an efficient and timely process, and conclusion of the proceedings.
rule_question: Is a person or body that has a direct or indirect interest in acquired or requisitioned property or its compensation (such as a beneficiary bearing the compensation, a purchaser, decree-holder, tenant, allottee or administrator) treated as a person interested, with standing to be joined, to receive notice, to lead evidence and to challenge adverse orders or awards?
rule_statement: Where a person (especially a beneficiary that bears the compensation) has a direct or indirect interest in acquired property or its compensation, the inclusive and liberally construed definition of 'person interested' and the related statutory and writ remedies give it standing. It may be joined, receive notice, adduce evidence and challenge an adverse determination, and a determination made without hearing it cannot bind it. The bar on a beneficiary company or authority demanding a reference under s.18 (proviso to s.50(2)) does not remove these rights.

test_issue: A lease challenged by pending proceedings remained subsisting on the appointed day despite the tenants’ interim loss of physical possession.
rule_question: Does an existing tenancy or subordinate interest continue despite an intervening event (partial acquisition of the reversion, merger of interests, statutory abolition or vesting, a termination notice or pending possession proceeding, a third-party title suit, or wrongful dispossession) that does not satisfy the legally prescribed requirements for ending it?
rule_statement: An existing tenancy or subordinate interest is not ended by a partial acquisition of the reversion, a unity of holding of non-higher/lower interests, abolition or vesting, a termination notice or pending proceeding, a third-party title suit, or wrongful dispossession, unless the legally prescribed mode of termination is completed or a clear intention or an operative statutory provision ends it. The tenant's statutory rights and obligations therefore continue.
rule_if: existing_tenancy_or_subordinate_interest and intervening_event_occurred and not event_satisfies_legal_requirements_for_termination and not clear_intention_or_express_statutory_provision_ending_interest

test_issue: The compensation for land acquired under the subsequent notification was properly determined by applying a cumulative increase to the compensation fixed for the earlier acquisition.
rule_question: Where land is acquired under a later notification and an earlier determination of market value exists for comparable land (or land acquired for the same purpose), may the earlier value be increased to account for escalation in land prices over the intervening period?
rule_statement: When the market value of later-acquired land is assessed from a benchmark value fixed for comparable or same-purpose land acquired earlier, the court may increase that benchmark to reflect price escalation over the intervening period. The rate varies, e.g. an annual percentage or a fixed percentage uplift, and depends on the facts.

test_issue: A cross-objection may challenge the legality and validity of a compromise decree under the applicable provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure.
rule_question: Can a party challenge an earlier interlocutory order (including a non-terminating remand order or other intermediate ruling) in an appeal from the final decree, order or judgment, even if no appeal lay from it or an available appeal was not taken when it was made?
rule_statement: A non-terminating interlocutory order may be challenged in an appeal from the final decision in the same proceeding, whether no appeal lay from it or an available appeal was not taken, unless a statute expressly bars the challenge. Such orders are not treated as finally closing the issue, although they may bind the lower courts until set aside.

test_issue: A refusal to grant sanction does not justify quashing the entire complaint and chargesheet where the alleged conduct may fall outside official duties, particularly when other accused persons are also charged.
rule_question: Can a High Court, in exercise of its inherent or writ jurisdiction, quash an FIR, investigation, charge-sheet or criminal proceeding at the threshold where the allegations, taken at face value, disclose an offence and the accused's defence, the reliability of the allegations or the accused's involvement depends on disputed facts or evidence that has yet to be collected or tested?
rule_statement: A court exercising inherent or writ jurisdiction to quash criminal proceedings must examine the allegations and material at face value and must not weigh evidence, test reliability, or decide disputed defences. Where the allegations disclose an offence and the outcome depends on disputed facts or incomplete investigation, and no exceptional ground is made out, the proceeding must continue.
rule_if: criminal_proceeding_quashing_challenge and allegations_taken_at_face_value_disclose_offence and (truth_reliability_or_defence_depends_on_disputed_facts_or_evidence or investigation_incomplete) and not exceptional_ground_for_quashing_made_out

test_issue: A court exercising appellate jurisdiction under Section 37 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 cannot reappraise the merits of an arbitral award or exceed the limits of interference applicable under Section 34.
rule_question: When a statute refers a compensation dispute to an arbitrator and gives an appeal from the award to the High Court, is the High Court's decision on that appeal an arbitral award that cannot be appealed further as an ordinary civil judgment, decree or order, or through inherited leave jurisdiction?
rule_statement: Where a statute sends a dispute to an arbitrator and provides an appeal to the High Court, that appeal continues the arbitration. The High Court's decision remains an award, not a judgment, decree or order of a court in its ordinary civil jurisdiction. It is therefore not appealable under the ordinary civil appeal provisions, and the inherited leave power, which is limited to civil-case judgments, cannot be used.
rule_if: statutory_arbitration_reference and appeal_from_arbitrator_award_to_high_court_under_statute and appeal_continues_arbitration_proceeding and not high_court_acting_in_ordinary_civil_jurisdiction

test_issue: A later sale deed and stamp duty paid on it do not eliminate the liability to pay the required stamp duty on an earlier agreement to sell that is the principal instrument.
rule_question: Does a mortgagor's (or successor's) right to redeem a mortgage survive, and may it still be enforced, where no legally recognised mode of extinguishment (a completed registered conveyance, a final decree or order barring redemption, agreement, merger, or a statutory bar) has taken effect, despite an auction, an agreement for sale, a pending or unfinalised sale, long possession or a mortgagee's acquisition of other rights?
rule_statement: A mortgagor's right of redemption ends only by a legally recognised means, such as agreement, merger, a decree, a completed registered conveyance, a final sale or a statutory bar. An auction, an agreement for sale, an unfinalised or appealed sale, a decree for sale that was not executed, long possession by the mortgagee, or the mortgagee's acquisition of a related grant or estate does not by itself extinguish it.

test_issue: A court must refer a dispute to arbitration under Section 8 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act when the dispute is covered by a valid arbitration clause.
rule_question: Does a broadly worded arbitration clause in a principal agreement extend to disputes under related, ancillary or substituted agreements that are integrally connected to it, so that the connected disputes may be referred to and decided in one arbitration?
rule_statement: Where a principal agreement contains a broad arbitration clause and the disputes arise under related, ancillary or substituted agreements that are integrally connected with it, the clause governs the connected disputes and they may be referred together and resolved in one arbitration.

test_issue: A sale deed executed after the first acquisition notification could not be relied on to determine compensation for a subsequent acquisition of land in the same villages.
rule_question: Can a person who is not the owner or a successful party at the relevant time (a purchaser or transferee after the acquisition notification, or a non-objector or non-party relying on others' successful challenges or on defects affecting others) challenge the acquisition or claim title, policy benefits or relief against the acquiring State, or is such a person limited to compensation through the former owner?
rule_statement: A post-notification purchaser or transferee takes no title enforceable against the State and cannot challenge the acquisition or claim owner-linked benefits, though it may claim compensation through the vendor. Likewise, persons who filed no objections or were not parties cannot take advantage of another owner's successful but individualised challenge, or of defects affecting others' interests, unless the acquisition was quashed in its entirety.

test_issue: A court considering bail under Section 43D(5) of the UAPA must examine the charge-sheet material as a whole, taken as it is, to determine whether reasonable grounds exist for believing the accusations are prima facie true, without conducting a mini-trial.
rule_question: At the pre-charge or discharge stage, what standard must a court apply to the prosecution material in deciding whether to discharge the accused or to frame a charge and send the accused for trial?
rule_statement: At the discharge or charge stage the court only sifts the material to see whether a prima facie case exists, without a mini trial or a decision on the merits. If the material at face value discloses the offence ingredients or a prima facie case (or grave suspicion), discharge is wrong and the accused must stand trial.

test_issue: An insult or intimidation attracts the provision only when it is directed at a person because of that person’s caste or tribe, and the charge-sheet must set out the alleged utterances sufficiently to permit the court to assess whether the offence is made out.
rule_question: At a preliminary stage (anticipatory bail or the magistrate's decision whether to issue process), should the court confine itself to a prima facie assessment of whether the complaint or evidence discloses the offence, rather than critically weighing the evidence as at trial?
rule_statement: At a preliminary stage, the court only checks whether the complaint or preliminary evidence prima facie discloses the offence. If it does, the court must apply the consequence the statute attaches (the bar on anticipatory bail, or issue of process and commitment to the Sessions Court), and must not appraise the evidence as if at trial.

test_issue: Delays in obtaining required approvals caused by government authorities, where the project developer acted diligently and was not negligent, qualify as a force majeure event under the power purchase agreement.
rule_question: Where a land acquisition authority has delayed unreasonably, whether in making awards, completing the acquisition or appointing an arbitrator, should the court quash the acquisition, or preserve it and grant additional or equitable monetary relief (additional compensation, solatium or interest) to the affected owners?
rule_statement: Unreasonable, unexplained delay by an acquisition authority does not by itself invalidate the acquisition, particularly where land has been developed, third-party interests have arisen, or the owners contributed to the delay. The court instead remedies the injury through additional compensation or equitable solatium or interest, using its writ or equitable powers even where the statute provides no such relief.

test_issue: Whether profane abuse, without an obscene utterance in or near a public place, constitutes an offence under Section 294(b) of the Indian Penal Code.
rule_question: When may a High Court or the Supreme Court, under its inherent power (Section 482 CrPC / Section 561-A CrPC 1898, and Article 142), quash criminal proceedings as an abuse of process or to secure the ends of justice?
rule_statement: Inherent power may be used, sparingly and with caution, to quash criminal proceedings where the allegations on their face disclose no offence, where a civil dispute has been given a criminal cloak and the prosecution is mala fide or intended to harass, where a bona fide settlement makes continuing a private-natured case futile, or where there is a legal bar, no legal evidence or bleak prospects of conviction.

test_issue: A resolution plan must recognize a creditor’s statutory charge over the corporate debtor’s assets and account for the creditor as a secured creditor.
rule_question: Where a statute makes tax dues a first charge on the defaulter's property, or expressly gives the tax recovery precedence over mortgage claims, does the State's claim take priority over a mortgage or other security interest, including one created earlier?
rule_statement: Where a statute expressly makes tax dues a first charge on the defaulter's property, or expressly gives tax recoverable as a public demand precedence over mortgage claims, the State's claim prevails over a mortgage, even one created earlier. A statutory charge reaches the whole property, not just the equity of redemption, and makes the State a secured creditor under the insolvency code.

test_issue: A person whose plot allotment remained unfinalized and who had not paid consideration was not protected by the exceptions to the quashing of discretionary-quota allotments.
rule_question: Does selection or success in a draw of lots for public land or housing, without a communicated (and where required, accepted) allotment, create an enforceable right to the plot or flat, or to its terms such as the price on the draw date?
rule_statement: A draw of lots is only a method of identifying a prospective allottee. It does not by itself give an enforceable right to allotment, possession or draw-date price. A right arises only when the allotment is officially communicated, and where required accepted, and the authority's disclaimers and scheme terms still apply.

test_issue: The bar on questioning the admission of an insufficiently stamped instrument applies only when the court has judicially determined its admissibility.
rule_question: Can a party reopen, in a later appeal, review, execution or fresh proceeding, a decision, finding or order that has already become final or was left unchallenged or was settled earlier between the same parties?
rule_statement: A party bound by an earlier decree, order or finding that has attained finality, or that it failed to challenge at the proper stage, cannot reopen it in a later appeal, execution, review or fresh proceeding. Courts exercising limited appellate or supervisory review also decline to reappraise concluded factual findings.
rule_if: later_proceeding_seeks_to_reopen_issue and issue_already_decided_by_prior_decision_or_finding and (prior_decision_became_final_or_challenge_was_dismissed or party_failed_to_challenge_it_at_available_stage_or_court_declines_to_reappraise_findings_in_limited_review) and same_party_bound_by_prior_decision

test_issue: An application raising objections to execution under Section 47 of the Code of Civil Procedure may be treated in substance as an application under Order XXI Rule 97 where the objection concerns obstruction to delivery of possession.
rule_question: In execution proceedings, when is a judgment-debtor or a person claiming through the debtor barred by actual or constructive res judicata from raising an objection later, having omitted, abandoned or failed to have it decided earlier?
rule_statement: Res judicata, including constructive res judicata, applies to execution proceedings, so a judgment-debtor who had notice and opportunity but omitted or abandoned an objection in earlier proceedings that became final is barred from raising it later. It does not apply where the objection was never heard and finally decided, where the debtor was denied notice, where the party is not bound by the earlier decision, or where the failure concerns the court's authority to sell.
rule_if: execution_proceeding and objection_not_raised_or_pursued_earlier and (not no_opportunity_or_notice_was_denied) and (not objection_not_heard_and_finally_decided) and (not objection_goes_to_inherent_jurisdiction_to_sell_or_parties_not_bound) and earlier_orders_became_final

test_issue: A claim of title by adverse possession requires proof of open, continuous, and hostile possession.
rule_question: Does a party who seeks relief founded on title, possession or another asserted right bear the burden of proving that right, including the identity of the property, without relying on the opponent's failure to prove a competing title?
rule_statement: A party who asks the court for relief based on title or another asserted right must plead and prove the facts that make out that right, including the identity and location of the property and its own entitlement. It cannot succeed on the weakness or non-proof of the opponent's title, and a court errs by shifting the burden to the opponent.

test_issue: Acquired land used as a safety zone is not eligible for return under Section 101 of the 2013 Act when it has not remained unutilised for the prescribed period.
rule_question: Once land or a proprietary or intermediary interest in it has vested in the State (by completed acquisition or by land-reform, ceiling or surplus legislation), can the former owner or proprietor recover possession, restitution, reconveyance or related relief, or does the vesting bar the claim?
rule_statement: Once land or a proprietary interest has validly vested in the State, whether through completed acquisition or through land-reform, ceiling or surplus legislation, the former owner cannot recover possession, restitution, reconveyance or related relief. This holds even if the land is unused, put to another public purpose, or not yet used, unless a statutory saving or a statutory reconveyance condition is satisfied.

test_issue: A party who admits signing an agreement but alleges coercion or threat bears the burden of proving that allegation.
rule_question: When the execution or genuineness of a document is disputed, which party bears the burden of proof, and can that burden be shifted to the opposing party merely because of a denial, possession of the document, or the difficulty of proving a negative?
rule_statement: The burden of proof follows the party asserting the affirmative. A party relying on a document whose execution is denied must prove its execution, and a plaintiff who sues alleging forgery bears the initial burden of proving it. The opposing party need not prove the negative, and possession of the document or difficulty of proof does not shift the burden unless a fiduciary or dominant-party relationship is established.

test_issue: A certified copy of a registered sale deed admissible under the applicable statutory provisions does not require proof through an independent witness or recourse to the presumptions under Sections 90 and 110 of the Evidence Act.
rule_question: When the original document is not produced, on what conditions may secondary evidence of its contents be admitted, and what must the offering party show first?
rule_statement: Secondary evidence of a document is admissible only if the original is not produced, the non-production is accounted for on a ground the Evidence Act permits, a factual foundation is laid, and the copy is shown to be a true one. A bare copy, or a certified copy tendered without any explanation for the original's absence, is not enough. Where the foundation is incomplete or has not been examined, the party may be given the chance to lay it.
rule_if: secondary_evidence_offered and original_not_produced and nonproduction_accounted_for_on_permitted_ground and factual_foundation_established and copy_shown_to_be_true_copy

test_issue: The twin conditions for bail under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act do not displace the principle that bail is the rule and jail is the exception, and prolonged pre-trial incarceration with no likelihood of a timely trial may justify conditional liberty consistently with Article 21.
rule_question: When may an appellate court (including the Supreme Court under Article 136) set aside or cancel a grant of bail because the granting court exercised its discretion without applying its mind to material evidence, the gravity of the offence and the risks to the trial?
rule_statement: An appellate court may set aside a grant of bail in a serious case where the material shows prima facie involvement and the granting court acted arbitrarily, either by ignoring relevant material or giving no case-specific reasons, or by disregarding a substantiated risk to witnesses or the fair trial. Such review of the correctness of the grant does not require proof of later misuse of bail.
rule_if: appeal_challenges_bail_grant and serious_offence_alleged and prima_facie_material_against_accused and (granting_court_ignored_material_or_gave_no_case_specific_reasons or substantiated_risk_to_witnesses_or_fair_trial_disregarded)

test_issue: Failure to submit a change report within the prescribed period does not automatically invalidate a person’s assumption of office as a trust administrator or the underlying change in the trust.
rule_question: Does a procedural shortfall in an adjudicatory or administrative process (non-supply of a report, no personal hearing, non-use of an opportunity, or non-filing of objections) amount to a denial of natural justice that invalidates the resulting decision, or does it depend on whether the affected party had a fair opportunity and suffered prejudice?
rule_statement: Natural justice is flexible and context-dependent. An omission such as not supplying a report, not holding a personal hearing, or a party's failure to use an offered opportunity does not by itself invalidate a decision where the party had a fair opportunity to present its case and showed no prejudice, other defect or mala fides.

test_issue: A conviction based on circumstantial evidence is sustainable where the proved circumstances form a complete chain that excludes reasonable hypotheses consistent with innocence.
rule_question: When can a criminal conviction resting on circumstantial evidence be sustained, and when must it be set aside, in light of the requirement that the proved circumstances form a complete chain consistent only with guilt and excluding every reasonable hypothesis of innocence?
rule_statement: A conviction based on circumstantial evidence is sustainable only if every incriminating circumstance is fully proved and together they form a complete chain pointing only to the accused's guilt and excluding every reasonable hypothesis of innocence. If a material circumstance is unproved, the chain has a gap, or a reasonable innocent explanation remains, the conviction cannot stand, because suspicion, however strong, is no substitute for proof.

test_issue: A non-party cannot obtain a blanket clarification of a prior judgment through intervention in proceedings to which the non-party was not a participant.
rule_question: When does an earlier decision, order or proceeding fail to operate as res judicata, constructive res judicata or issue estoppel in a later proceeding?
rule_statement: Res judicata and its extensions (constructive res judicata, issue estoppel) apply only where the same matter was directly and substantially in issue and was heard and finally decided between the same parties or those claiming under them. They do not apply where the earlier case involved different property, parties, issues or cause of action, ended without a final merits decision, or decided only a pure question of law or jurisdiction.

test_issue: The punishment for contempt, including confinement in civil prison, may be modified in light of the contemnor’s age and circumstances.
rule_question: When may a criminal court, on sentencing or appeal, award compensation to a victim or the victim's dependants under Section 357 CrPC (alone or alongside a reduced sentence), and what must it consider in deciding whether to order it and how much?
rule_statement: Under Section 357 CrPC, a trial or appellate court may order compensation to a victim or dependants in addition to other sentences. The amount must be reasonable given the nature of the crime, the injury, the justness of the claim and the offender's ability to pay. Where circumstances justify it, such as time already served, the court may reduce imprisonment to the period undergone, with default enforced by imprisonment or revival of the original sentence.

test_issue: A statutory board cannot transfer acquired land without the required statutory sanction or return it when it has not obtained title through a conveyance from the Government.
rule_question: When is a compulsory land acquisition, or an action built on it, invalid because the power was used for an extraneous or private purpose, or because the notification or procedure did not meet the statutory requirements for the stated purpose?
rule_statement: A compulsory acquisition, and actions founded on it, are invalid where the acquisition power is used for an extraneous, colourable or private-benefit purpose. They are equally invalid where the notification or procedure fails the statutory requirements for the stated purpose, such as adequate disclosure and description, the correct company or public-purpose route, or a proper statutory basis for each component.

test_issue: Beneficiaries of transactions made in contempt have no right to be impleaded or heard in contempt proceedings merely because they claim to be bona fide purchasers for value without notice.
rule_question: What is the effect of a transfer of an interest in property made while litigation over that property is pending (lis pendens): is the transferee's claim subordinate to the rights determined in the litigation, and does the transfer give the transferee any independent right, equity or entitlement to be joined in the suit?
rule_statement: A transfer of property made while litigation over it is pending does not defeat or override the rights determined in that litigation. The transferee is bound by the result and takes no title where the transferor had none. The transferee has no automatic right to be impleaded and cannot rely on the transfer to build adverse possession or take inconsistent stands. Knowledge or good faith does not change this, though the transferee may have private remedies against the transferor.

test_issue: Criminal proceedings may be quashed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure when the allegations, accepted in their entirety, do not prima facie constitute an offence.
rule_question: When may a High Court or the Supreme Court, under its inherent power (Section 482 CrPC / Section 561-A CrPC 1898, and Article 142), quash criminal proceedings as an abuse of process or to secure the ends of justice?
rule_statement: Inherent power may be used, sparingly and with caution, to quash criminal proceedings where the allegations on their face disclose no offence, where a civil dispute has been given a criminal cloak and the prosecution is mala fide or intended to harass, where a bona fide settlement makes continuing a private-natured case futile, or where there is a legal bar, no legal evidence or bleak prospects of conviction.

test_issue: Statutory provisions permitting assignment or alienation of public land do not authorize allotments that violate the equality guarantee in Article 14.
rule_question: Does a land-related law, tax, compensation scheme or State action in acquisition, release or withdrawal violate the equality guarantee of Article 14 when it treats similarly situated persons or properties differently (or dissimilar ones alike) without an intelligible differentia that has a rational relation to the object of the law?
rule_statement: Under Article 14, a land-related law or State action is invalid if it treats similarly situated owners, parcels, properties or groups differently, or treats materially dissimilar ones alike, without an intelligible differentia that is rationally related to the law's object and without any justification from the State. Where the discrimination is in executive action (selective acquisition, release or withdrawal), the State must treat comparable owners consistently or the action is set aside.
rule_if: equality_challenge_to_land_related_law_or_state_action and (similarly_situated_persons_or_properties_treated_differently or dissimilar_persons_or_properties_treated_alike) and not (classification_rests_on_intelligible_differentia_with_rational_nexus_to_object) and no_valid_justification_shown_by_state

test_issue: A former director or promoter’s past relationship with a corporate debtor does not, without a continuing connection to its business, make an auction purchaser ineligible as a related party under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
rule_question: Can an electricity supplier refuse or condition a new supply or connection to an auction purchaser of premises on payment of the previous consumer's or owner's electricity arrears, where the purchaser is a distinct third party who did not assume those arrears?
rule_statement: Electricity arrears are a contractual liability of the former consumer and are not a charge on the premises. An auction purchaser who is a distinct third party and has not assumed the arrears cannot be made to pay them as a condition of a new supply, unless an applicable statutory rule or binding term of supply authorizes it.
rule_if: purchaser_acquired_premises_at_auction_or_sale and purchaser_seeks_new_or_fresh_supply and purchaser_distinct_from_prior_consumer and not purchaser_assumed_prior_arrears and not binding_supply_rule_authorizes_recovery_from_purchaser

test_issue: The later award of compensation to affected individuals omitted from the original assessment is valid and does not violate procedural fairness or applicable rules.
rule_question: Once a compensation determination, payment or related direction in land-acquisition matters has become final or been satisfied at an earlier stage, can it be reopened, recalled or reappropriated in later proceedings (reference, appeal, execution or fresh acquisition proceedings)?
rule_statement: Compensation determinations, directions and payments in land acquisition that have become final or been satisfied at an earlier stage bind the parties and cannot be reopened, reappropriated or paid again in later reference, appellate, execution or acquisition proceedings. Only later enhancements or components, or jurisdictionally void orders, can be addressed afresh.
rule_if: land_compensation_matter_in_later_proceeding and earlier_compensation_determination_or_payment_final_or_satisfied and later_proceeding_seeks_to_reopen_or_reallocate_that_earlier_matter and not (earlier_matter_void_for_want_of_jurisdiction or court_expressly_directs_otherwise)

test_issue: The 25% deposit requirement under Rule 9(3) of the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002 is met when the purchaser deposits that amount on the day of auction or by the next working day.
rule_question: When a judgment-debtor applies under Order XXI Rule 89 CPC to set aside an execution sale, must the required deposit be made within 30 days of the sale (Order XXI Rule 92(2)), or is a deposit made within the longer 60-day application period under Article 127 of the Limitation Act sufficient?
rule_statement: On the view taken by two of the three members, Order XXI Rule 92(2) is harmonised with Article 127 of the Limitation Act. An application and the required deposit made within the 60-day application period are not defeated because the deposit came after 30 days, and the sale may be set aside. One member (1672592_1 treated as discretionary) frames the outcome as the court's discretion rather than an entitlement. The third member takes the opposite view.

test_issue: A legal heir with an interest in disputed property may be impleaded as a party to the suit so that all necessary parties can be heard before the court decides the dispute.
rule_question: Must a person who is not the direct party to an administrative or statutory proceeding, but whose interests (possessory, tenancy, beneficiary or bidder interests) may be adversely affected by its outcome, be given notice and an opportunity to be heard before the decision is made?
rule_statement: Natural justice, or the statute's own hearing requirement, entitles a person with a real interest in the subject matter, such as a beneficiary, a company, a tenant in possession or a provisionally accepted bidder, to notice and a hearing before a decision that may prejudice that interest. An order passed without hearing that person is vitiated and the matter is reconsidered afresh, even if the person has no complete legal right.

rule_question: Can a person claim a statutory tenancy or sub-tenancy protection (security of tenure, protected-tenant or occupancy status, or protection from eviction) when the governing statute expressly or by its definition excludes the claimant's class, the lessor, or the land from that protection?
rule_statement: Statutory tenancy protections are available only to those within the class, lessor type, land and time period the statute covers. A claimant who is a trespasser, a prohibited sub-lessee, a disqualified tenant, or who deals with an excluded lessor or land, or who relies on a lapsed enactment, cannot invoke the protection. Saving provisions do not override an express exclusion.
rule_if: claim_for_statutory_tenancy_protection and (claimant_is_excluded_class_under_statute or lessor_or_land_excluded_from_statute or protection_law_no_longer_in_force)
typical_outcome: In all 7 members the protection claim fails. In 1 member (1882913_1) the exclusion also lets the landlord take possession of the entire leased land.

rule_question: Does a later-enacted law or amendment restricting, invalidating or deeming the effect of transfers apply to a transfer completed before that law took effect, where the law is not expressly retrospective?
rule_statement: A statute or amendment that restricts, invalidates or deems the effect of transfers operates prospectively unless it says otherwise. It does not reach a transfer completed before it came into force, and that transfer is judged under the law then in force.
typical_outcome: In all five covered members the later provision was held not to apply to the earlier transfer, which survived. The sixth member (outlier) read down a recovery law to protect perfected titles.

rule_question: When does possession of immovable property, held openly, continuously and in hostility to the claimant's title for the full limitation period, ripen into title by adverse possession or prescription and bar the former owner's claim?
rule_statement: A person who possesses immovable property actually, openly, continuously and without permission, as owner and hostilely to the true owner's title, for the full limitation period acquires title by adverse possession. The former owner's right is then extinguished and a later suit for possession or recovery is barred. The possessor must plead and prove these elements, and mere long possession is not enough.
typical_outcome: In all 11 members, adverse possession or prescription was held established, title vested in the possessor, and the claimant's suit was barred or its claim failed. The one member that is a general statement of requirements (199096823_2) sets out the elements without deciding a dispute on its facts.

rule_question: Is a recorded conversation on an electronic or magnetic medium (tape or compact disc) a document or evidence that can be received, and on what conditions (relevance, voice identification, proof of accuracy and absence of tampering) is it admissible?
rule_statement: A recorded conversation on a tape or compact disc is a document or electronic record within the Evidence Act. It can be received in evidence if it is relevant, the speakers' voices are identified, and its accuracy and integrity are proved so that tampering is excluded.
rule_if: recorded_conversation_on_medium and conversation_relevant and speaker_voices_identified and recording_accuracy_and_integrity_proved
typical_outcome: All 3 members treat recorded conversations as receivable evidence or documents: 2 hold them admissible once the conditions are met, and 1 holds that a compact disc is a document.

rule_question: When is a will proved or accepted as genuine, and when does the propounder fail to prove it? This turns on the statutory execution and attestation requirements, the testator's capacity and free volition, and whether any suspicious circumstances are real and have been satisfactorily explained.
rule_statement: The propounder of a will must prove its execution and attestation as required by Section 63 of the Succession Act and Section 68 of the Evidence Act, and must prove the testator's capacity and free volition. Where genuine suspicious circumstances exist, the propounder must also remove them to the court's satisfaction. If this is done and the challenger does not prove fraud, coercion or undue influence, the will is upheld. If the attestation evidence fails, or real suspicions remain unexplained, the will is not proved.
rule_if: will_contested_proceeding and propounder_proves_due_execution_and_attestation_through_available_attesting_witness_as_required_by_law and propounder_proves_testamentary_capacity_and_free_volition and (no_genuine_suspicious_circumstances_remain or suspicious_circumstances_satisfactorily_explained) and challenger_fails_to_prove_fraud_coercion_or_undue_influence
typical_outcome: Of the 25 members, about 18 uphold or find the will proved. About 6 reject it or hold it not proved, for failed attestation proof or unresolved suspicion. A few members (1740276_1, 1928029_2, 1932982_1) only state that the propounder must remove suspicion, in a framework that precedes the final finding.

rule_question: Where mining leases are granted under a statutory scheme (the MMDR Act and the Mineral Concession Rules, or equivalent state rules), must the authority decide applications only through the prescribed notification and criteria, so that extra-statutory considerations such as past investment, past State commitments, equity, or applications filed outside the prescribed notice cannot decide the grant?
rule_statement: Where a statute and rules govern the grant of mining leases, the State acts as a statutory delegate and must follow the prescribed notification procedure and criteria. Past investment, past commitments, equity, or applications made outside the required notification cannot displace them, and a recommendation or consideration contrary to the scheme is invalid.
typical_outcome: All 8 members hold that the statutory scheme controls. The non-statutory preference or recommendation is invalid (1220288_1, _5, _6, _7, 93595604_5), and applications filed outside the notification process are not entertained (1201771_3, 1220288_2, _3).

rule_question: How is a temple or religious endowment classified as public or private, and what evidence of dedication, public worship as of right, management and support establishes public character?
rule_statement: A temple or religious endowment is public where the founder intended, or the circumstances show dedication to, the public or a section of it, as shown by public worship as of right or without interference, long public use, public or royal support, and management as trustees. Family management, a restriction on entry for orderly worship, or a residential appearance does not defeat this. The claimant of private character must rebut any presumption and prove it.
rule_if: religious_institution_classification_dispute and not private_status_established_by_claimant and (founder_intended_worship_for_public_or_section or public_worship_as_of_right_or_without_interference or long_public_use) and (public_contributions_or_grants_or_property_in_deity_name or management_not_treated_as_private_ownership or public_temple_presumption_applies)
typical_outcome: About 10 of 15 members hold the institution public on the cumulative evidence. Two hold it private or not a public temple (1292955_1, 1864792_1). Three are procedural, definitional or abstract (1896039_1, 1504501_2, 740772_4); the first two of these also favour public or institutional status.

rule_question: When does an appellate court sustain a conviction for attempted murder under Section 307 IPC, and when must it reduce or alter the conviction to a lesser offence (such as hurt or grievous hurt by a dangerous weapon) or decline to convict, depending on whether intention or knowledge to cause death is established from the weapon, the injury, the part of the body targeted and the surrounding circumstances?
rule_statement: A Section 307 IPC conviction stands where the intention or knowledge required for murder is inferred from the circumstances (weapon, body part, severity of injury) and an overt act by the identified accused is proved. Where that intention is not established, or the accused is not tied to the grievous injury, the conviction is altered to a lesser offence such as Section 324 or 326 IPC, or an acquittal is not disturbed.
typical_outcome: Of 8 issues, 3 uphold Section 307 IPC (115651329_1, 273583_3, 531211_5), the last two with a sentence reduction. 4 alter the conviction to a lesser offence (Section 324 or 326 IPC, or abetment thereof) with reduced sentences (1086707_3, _4, _5, 234452_4). 1 leaves an acquittal undisturbed (212245_1).

rule_question: When compensation for compulsorily acquired land is awarded or enhanced by a court, does it carry the statutory additions (solatium, additional amount and interest), and does the interest payable on compensation extend to the solatium and other additions?
rule_statement: Where a court fixes or enhances compensation for compulsorily acquired land, the claimant gets the statutory solatium and additional amount and interest on the compensation. Because solatium is part of compensation, the interest also runs on the solatium and cannot be split off to exclude it.
typical_outcome: All 14 covered members grant solatium and/or interest on the enhanced or awarded compensation. About 8 expressly hold that interest is payable on solatium or on all components, mostly following Sunder v. Union of India, which overruled Prem Nath Kapur. About 5 simply direct the usual solatium and interest without citing authority.

rule_question: Where a State legislature has transferred the subject of ceilings on urban immovable property to Parliament under Article 252, how is the field divided between the parliamentary urban ceiling law and the State agricultural ceiling law for land within or outside urban agglomerations?
rule_statement: After an Article 252 transfer, the parliamentary law governs ceilings on urban land within covered urban agglomerations, and the State ceiling law is displaced to that extent. The State law is not wholly invalid: it continues to govern agricultural land that the parliamentary law excludes and areas not yet designated as urban agglomerations.
rule_if: state_resolution_under_article_252_transferred_urban_ceiling_subject_to_parliament and parliamentary_ceiling_law_covers_designated_urban_agglomerations and state_agricultural_ceiling_law_exists and ((land_is_within_covered_urban_agglomeration and not land_is_excluded_agricultural_land_under_parliamentary_law) or (land_is_agricultural_or_outside_covered_urban_agglomeration))
typical_outcome: All 3 hold that the field is divided by the Article 252 transfer. The parliamentary law governs covered urban land (2 members). The State law survives for agricultural land excluded by the parliamentary law, or for areas not yet designated (2 members, with overlap).

rule_question: Must lands acquired together, in the same village or under the same notification, be given a uniform rate of compensation, or may different rates or belts be fixed where the lands differ materially in location, quality, access, potential or legal restrictions on use?
rule_statement: Lands that are acquired together, form one block, lie in the same village or are covered by the same notification need not receive the same compensation. Where differences in location, quality, access, potential or use restrictions affect market value, the court may classify the lands, or divide them into belts, and fix different rates. A uniform rate applied without regard to such differences is erroneous.
typical_outcome: In all 8 members the claim for a uniform rate was rejected, and different rates, belts or categories were upheld or directed. In 2 members (1771435_1, 845284_2) a uniform rate applied by the High Court was set aside as erroneous.

rule_question: Under section 171 of the Income-tax Act, 1961, can a previously assessed Hindu undivided family be treated as partitioned for income-tax purposes where the property has not been divided in the manner its nature permits (physical division if it admits of it), even though there is a severance of status, an agreement or decree, or a division of income?
rule_statement: For income-tax purposes a previously assessed Hindu undivided family is treated as partitioned only if the claimant proves the division of property that section 171 and its Explanation require, namely physical division where the property admits of it, or the fullest division it admits otherwise. Severance of status under Hindu law, an agreement or preliminary decree, allocation of undivided shares and division of income are not enough.
typical_outcome: In all 3 members the claim of partition was rejected for tax purposes and the family continued to be treated as undivided.

rule_question: Does long and continuous cohabitation of a man and woman as spouses give rise to a rebuttable presumption of a valid marriage, and so of the legitimacy of their children, and when is that presumption treated as rebutted or not rebutted?
rule_statement: Where a man and woman have cohabited continuously for a long time as husband and wife and no insurmountable legal obstacle to marriage is shown, the law presumes a valid marriage rather than concubinage, and presumes the children legitimate. The presumption is rebuttable, but only by clear and unimpeachable evidence. Omissions in family documents or witness evidence that does not deny cohabitation do not rebut it.
rule_if: prolonged_continuous_cohabitation_as_spouses and not insurmountable_obstacle_to_marriage and not unimpeachable_rebuttal_evidence
typical_outcome: In 6 of 7 members the presumption of marriage and legitimacy was upheld or restored because it was not rebutted, usually restoring the first appellate or trial court's decree. In 1 member (1388066_1) the presumption was held rebutted on the cumulative evidence and the claim failed.

rule_question: Once issuance or signature of a cheque is admitted or proved in a cheque-dishonour prosecution, do the presumptions under Sections 118(a) and 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act continue to operate until the accused rebuts them by a probable defence supported by evidence or circumstances, and what follows if the accused does or does not do so?
rule_statement: Admission or proof of a cheque's issuance or signature raises rebuttable presumptions of consideration and debt under Sections 118(a) and 139. The presumptions persist until the accused establishes a probable defence on a preponderance of probabilities, which he may do through the whole evidence without testifying. Once rebutted, the burden returns to the complainant. If the accused has not rebutted, the presumptions remain, and disputed factual defences needing evidence are not a ground to quash the complaint at the threshold.
typical_outcome: Presumptions are applied in favour of the complainant. In 2 of 3 members the presumptions remained unrebutted (the complaint was restored for trial; the conviction was upheld). In 1 of 3 a probable, evidence-supported defence rebutted them and the acquittal was restored.

rule_question: Can a person in actual or settled possession of property obtain protection (injunction, restoration, or defence) against forcible or extra-legal dispossession, without proving title, so that anyone claiming a better right must recover possession through due process of law?
rule_statement: A person in actual or settled possession is protected against forcible, self-help or executive dispossession by someone who has not established a better title or lawful authority. Even a true owner must recover possession through due process, and the possessory remedy is granted without finally deciding title.
typical_outcome: About 23 of 25 members protect the possessor, by injunction, interim protection, restoration, quashing of executive action or a right of private defence, and leave title open. One (349194_2) is an outlier on a different point.

rule_question: Where a lease of immovable property falls within the categories that must be registered (year to year, term exceeding one year, or reserving yearly rent) and the document is unregistered, can the document be used to create the lease, prove it, or prove its terms, including as 'collateral' evidence?
rule_statement: An unregistered document of a lease that requires compulsory registration cannot create the lease or be used to prove the lease or any of its terms, such as rent, occupancy restrictions or subletting permissions. Describing a term as collateral does not avoid this, because the Section 49 proviso covers only a truly independent or divisible collateral transaction.
rule_if: lease_document_unregistered and lease_requires_compulsory_registration and document_offered_to_create_prove_or_establish_lease_or_its_terms and not collateral_transaction_exception_applies
typical_outcome: In 6 of 7 members the unregistered lease document was held inadmissible or ineffective to create or prove the lease or its terms, and the collateral-purpose argument was rejected where the term was part of the lease. In 1 of 7 a lease shorter than one year was held not compulsorily registrable.

rule_question: Where a structure is built or land is used in breach of a statutory restriction (environmental, forest or planning) and without the required permission or approval, may the authorities order its removal, and will the court uphold that order?
rule_statement: A structure built or a land use made inside a statutorily restricted area (coastal no-development zone, scheduled-road or controlled area, forest land) without the permission or approval the statute requires, or beyond what was approved, is unauthorized. Courts uphold orders for its removal or demolition and do not let technical pleas or delay defeat the statutory purpose.
typical_outcome: All 3 members uphold removal or demolition of the unauthorized structure.

rule_question: Is a person or body that has a direct or indirect interest in acquired or requisitioned property or its compensation (such as a beneficiary bearing the compensation, a purchaser, decree-holder, tenant, allottee or administrator) treated as a person interested, with standing to be joined, to receive notice, to lead evidence and to challenge adverse orders or awards?
rule_statement: Where a person (especially a beneficiary that bears the compensation) has a direct or indirect interest in acquired property or its compensation, the inclusive and liberally construed definition of 'person interested' and the related statutory and writ remedies give it standing. It may be joined, receive notice, adduce evidence and challenge an adverse determination, and a determination made without hearing it cannot bind it. The bar on a beneficiary company or authority demanding a reference under s.18 (proviso to s.50(2)) does not remove these rights.
typical_outcome: In all 22 members standing was upheld in favour of the interested person: roughly 15 concern beneficiary bodies (joinder, notice, evidence, appeal or challenge, or an award reopened), and about 7 concern purchasers, decree-holders, tenants, lessees, allottees and custodians who were held to have standing or to be persons interested.

rule_question: Under the transitional provision of the 2013 land acquisition statute (Section 24(2)), when are acquisition proceedings begun under the 1894 Act deemed to have lapsed because an award was made at least five years before the 2013 Act commenced? In particular, must both possession and payment have failed, or is either failure enough?
rule_statement: Where an award under the 1894 Act was made at least five years before the 2013 Act commenced, and possession was not taken and compensation was not paid or validly deposited in court, the acquisition is deemed to have lapsed under Section 24(2). Where only one of the two failures is present, the members split. Decisions following Pune Municipal Corporation v. Harakchand Misirimal Solanki treat either failure as enough. The Indore Development Authority line requires both failures, so lapse does not occur once possession has been taken.
rule_if: section_24_2_proceeding and award_at_least_five_years_before_commencement and possession_not_taken and compensation_not_paid
typical_outcome: Of the 15 covered members, 12 find deemed lapse, with the notification quashed or the appeal by the authority dismissed. Three (49625991_1, 49625991_3 and 88855536_1) hold that lapse requires both failures and that no lapse occurs once possession is taken, with interest payable on unpaid compensation. The cluster is inconsistent on whether either failure alone suffices.

rule_question: Can a conviction or finding of rape under Section 376 IPC be sustained where the evidence does not establish the offence, in particular the absence of consent, or leaves a reasonable view of consensual intercourse?
rule_statement: A conviction or finding of rape cannot stand unless the evidence proves the ingredients of the offence, notably intercourse without consent or against the woman's will. Evidence of mere intercourse, a mere possibility of rape, or a reasonable view of consensual intercourse (for a woman above the age of consent), and the absence of a charge, are not enough.
typical_outcome: All 3 members hold the rape finding or conviction unsustainable: one for no charge and no evidence, one for no evidence of lack of consent, one for benefit of doubt on a reasonably possible consensual view.

rule_question: Under Sections 5A and 6 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, is a landowner who has been heard in the objection inquiry entitled to a further hearing by the government after the collector's report is submitted and before the final acquisition declaration?
rule_statement: Where a landowner has been heard in the Section 5A objection inquiry and the officer's report and record go to the government, which considers them, no second hearing by the government is required before the Section 6 declaration. The report is recommendatory, and the government forms its own satisfaction on the record.
rule_if: land_acquisition_proceeding and objector_heard_in_section_5A_inquiry and report_and_objection_record_submitted_to_government and government_considered_report
typical_outcome: All 3 members hold that no further or second hearing is required after the report is submitted to the government.

rule_question: Can a claim or relief that is already barred by limitation, whether by a fresh suit or by a belated amendment of the pleadings, be sustained or allowed to relate back, so as to defeat the opposing party's accrued limitation right?
rule_statement: A suit or an amendment adding a new or distinct relief is barred where the limitation period, running from the claimant's actual or imputed knowledge of the triggering facts, had expired before it was brought. Courts refuse to let an amendment relate back to the original filing to defeat the opposing party's accrued limitation right, absent exceptional circumstances.
rule_if: (claimant_seeks_relief_by_suit_or_by_amendment_of_pleading) and relief_is_new_or_distinct_claim and limitation_period_for_that_relief_expired_before_it_was_sought and claimant_had_knowledge_or_notice_of_the_triggering_facts_earlier and not exceptional_circumstances_justifying_relation_back
typical_outcome: In all 10 covered members the time bar prevailed: 4 fresh suits were held barred (setting aside decree, specific performance, cancellation) and 6 belated amendments were refused or held not to relate back. Two further members (308216_2, 468319_2) refused amendments on non-limitation grounds.

rule_question: When a judge or bench of a High Court (or a smaller bench of the Supreme Court) disagrees with a binding decision of a coordinate or larger bench of the same court, must it follow that decision or refer the question to a larger bench, rather than depart from it or overrule it itself?
rule_statement: Under judicial propriety and discipline, a single judge or bench bound by an indistinguishable decision of a coordinate or larger bench of the same court must follow it. If it disagrees, it must refer the question to a larger bench, and may not overrule or ignore the decision itself, unless a higher court has overruled that decision directly or by necessary implication.
typical_outcome: In 8 of the 10 members, the later bench's departure from or overruling of binding precedent was held improper. It should have followed the precedent or referred the question to a larger bench (or, in one case, to the next larger bench rather than a five-judge bench). The other 2 members are outliers on separate procedural points.

rule_question: When may a court allow a review petition and correct or recall its earlier judgment because of an error in that judgment, including an error arising from overlooking a later or retrospective legal change?
rule_statement: A court may allow review and correct its earlier judgment where a clear error apparent on the record is shown. This includes the case where a retrospective or intervening amendment governing the matter was unavailable or overlooked and the error is evident without rehearing the issue.
rule_if: review_proceeding and (clear_error_apparent_on_record_shown or (later_or_retrospective_law_governs_matter and law_not_considered_in_original_decision and error_evident_from_record_without_rehearing))
typical_outcome: In all 3 members the review was allowed and the earlier judgment was corrected or reviewed.

rule_question: Once a compensation determination, payment or related direction in land-acquisition matters has become final or been satisfied at an earlier stage, can it be reopened, recalled or reappropriated in later proceedings (reference, appeal, execution or fresh acquisition proceedings)?
rule_statement: Compensation determinations, directions and payments in land acquisition that have become final or been satisfied at an earlier stage bind the parties and cannot be reopened, reappropriated or paid again in later reference, appellate, execution or acquisition proceedings. Only later enhancements or components, or jurisdictionally void orders, can be addressed afresh.
rule_if: land_compensation_matter_in_later_proceeding and earlier_compensation_determination_or_payment_final_or_satisfied and later_proceeding_seeks_to_reopen_or_reallocate_that_earlier_matter and not (earlier_matter_void_for_want_of_jurisdiction or court_expressly_directs_otherwise)
typical_outcome: About five of six members hold that the earlier final or satisfied matter cannot be reopened (finality, res judicata, no repeat compensation, no reappropriation). The sixth protects already-paid enhanced compensation from refund on fresh determination.
